title: Verifier-Guided Repair of LLM-Generated Vendor CLI Configurations: A Controlled Fault-Injection Paired Study
abstract: We test whether exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM-based repair workflow reduces residual unsafe or invalid vendor-CLI configurations compared with blind repair. In a preregistered controlled-challenge paired design (vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1) using adapter hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 and shared controlled-fault candidates, we planned 40 confirmatory pairs and observed 39 complete pairs (one source generation was invalid and excluded per preregistered rules). Baseline (blind repair) met the verifier+simulator acceptance predicate in 30/39 pairs (76.92%); guarded (verifier-guided) met it in 38/39 pairs (97.44%). Paired counts: n11 = 29, n10 = 9 (guarded-only), n01 = 1 (baseline-only), n00 = 0. The paired absolute difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.20512820512820507 (20.51 percentage points); two-sided exact paired test p = 0.021484375; 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359] (bootstrap resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). Execution used declared_model_version = gpt-5-mini and consumed 118 hosted-model calls (<= planned maximum 120). A preregistered harmful-overrepair confirmatory aggregation was not produced by the archived confirmatory executor; we document the exact archived artifacts and transformation mapping required to reproduce that preregistered safety statistic and treat it as unresolved for the confirmatory claim.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to assist NetOps tasks such as intent-to-configuration translation and automated remediation. A common safety-oriented architecture is generate–verify–repair (GVR): a deterministic verifier rejects candidates and exposes diagnostics that may guide a repair model to produce corrected artifacts. Prior empirical work in code and IaC domains reports that verifier-interposed repair can increase verifier pass rates while introducing costs and new failure modes [1]–[3]. Field surveys caution that read-oriented usefulness does not imply safe closed-loop changes without strong verification and conservative orchestration [5].

Motivation and research question. There is little controlled published evidence that quantifies verifier-guided repair effects on vendor CLI templates under preregistered, deterministic fault operators. A central methodological challenge is informativeness: the repair intervention can only operate when initial candidates trigger actionable diagnostics. We therefore designed a preregistered controlled-fault paired experiment with outcome-independent deterministic fault assignment and shared initial candidates to answer: Does exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow reduce residual unsafe or invalid vendor-CLI configurations compared with blind repair when confronted with preregistered controlled faults?
sections.related_work: Empirical generate–verify–repair (GVR) results demonstrate that deterministic verifiers can improve pass@1 and verifier-detected correctness on program and IaC tasks when verifier diagnostics are used as repair signals [1], [2]. Controlled analyses also document verifier-exploitation pathologies and recommend mitigations (multi-verifier ensembles, harmful-change constraints) for iterative refinement workflows [3]. Studies of verifier-mediated agent pipelines identify a measurable verifier "tax" (increased interaction horizon and compute), which affects operational cost–latency tradeoffs [4]. Surveys and demonstration-network case studies report that LLMs are often valuable for read-oriented NetOps assistance but highlight gaps when moving to closed-loop configuration changes [5]. These strands justify a controlled, preregistered, evidence-grounded experiment on vendor-CLI repair with deterministic faults and explicit harmful-change mappings.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study preregistration is vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, where success requires both the deterministic vendor-CLI verifier and a simulator-based compliance agreement. The preregistration SHA-256 is recorded in the execution manifest (preregistration_sha256 = 0ba66573928647f008b2cd5b9dde6708a61ae86ece55b693ace534e01e2b132c).

Execution contract and pairing semantics. Confirmatory execution used adapter hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 under shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics: for each preregistered task index a single deterministic controlled-fault candidate (deterministic_netops_fault_injector_v1) was generated and reused unchanged by both arms. Each pair received exactly one initial generation and one repair opportunity per condition; baseline denotes blind repair (no verifier diagnostics exposed) and guarded denotes repair with deterministic validator diagnostics exposed. The adapter-mandated confirmatory task_count was fixed at 40. The execution manifest records: started_at_utc = 2026-09-04T21:16:50.730326+00:00; completed_at_utc = 2026-09-04T21:19:34.370550+00:00; planned_episode_count = 80; completed_episode_count = 78; failed_episode_count = 2; model_calls_used = 118; maximum_model_calls = 120; source_generation_attempt_count = 40; source_valid_count = 39; source_invalid_or_failed_count = 1.

Model configuration and sampling records. The archived declared_model_version is gpt-5-mini and execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null (unset). Null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Per-call runtime sampling parameters and provider traces are archived and auditable at execution/execution_log.jsonl and execution/provider_calls/*.json; execution/model_configuration.json and execution/raw_results.jsonl are also available in the evidence bundle for inspection.

Controlled-challenge design and missingness. To ensure intervention activation we preregistered deterministic controlled faults (task indices 1..40) that inject actionable violations (examples: dropped_required_restore, protected_interface_change). Missingness rule 'complete_pair_primary' excludes a pair only if both condition episodes are unscorable; this occurred once (both_missing_pairs = 1). The analysis executor used exact paired binary testing (McNemar exact or equivalent) with a paired-bootstrap percentile CI (resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). Multiplicity handling: one predefined primary test; subgroup analyses are exploratory.

Scoring and harmful-change mapping. Primary success required agreement of the deterministic vendor-CLI validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) and a simulator-based compliance agreement. The preregistered harmful-change labeling used for the harmful-overrepair confirmatory hypothesis is implemented as an archived transformation: label an episode harmful if validation_after.violation_codes contains PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE or UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE. The transformation artifact is archived at execution/transformation_manifest.json and per-episode validator traces are in execution/scoring/*.json and execution/raw_results.jsonl.
sections.results:
Execution accounting. Planned confirmatory pairs = 40; completed episodes = 78 (39 complete pairs). Hosted-model calls used = 118. Source-generation attempts = 40 (39 valid, 1 invalid). The archived analysis artifacts include analysis/condition_summary.csv and analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (hashes in the evidence manifest).

Primary confirmatory outcomes (complete_pairs = 39). Baseline success = 30/39 = 0.7692307692307693. Guarded success = 38/39 = 0.9743589743589743. Paired contingency (guarded, baseline): n11 = 29, n10 = 9 (guarded-only), n01 = 1 (baseline-only), n00 = 0. Paired absolute difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.20512820512820507 (20.51 percentage points). Exact two-sided paired test p = 0.021484375. 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359] (bootstrap_resamples = 10000, bootstrap_seed = 1729).

Missingness and exclusions. One pair was excluded under 'complete_pair_primary' because the source generation was invalid; both condition episodes for that pair were unscorable (both_missing_pairs = 1). Per-episode terminal error reasons and execution logs are archived at execution/execution_log.jsonl and execution/raw_results.jsonl.

Preregistered harmful-overrepair confirmatory statistic: status and reproducibility path. The preregistration included a confirmatory safety hypothesis that guarded repair would not increase harmful over-repair by more than 5% absolute. The archived confirmatory analysis executor did not compute this aggregation (secondary_results = []). We therefore do not present a confirmatory harmful-overrepair result. The exact inputs needed to reproduce the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation are archived: (1) per-episode validation_after.violation_codes in execution/scoring/*.json and execution/raw_results.jsonl; (2) the harmful-change mapping transformation at execution/transformation_manifest.json (operational mapping: any validation_after.violation_codes containing PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE or UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE is harmful); (3) complete_pairs = 39 per analysis/missingness_summary.csv. Independent auditors can deterministically reproduce the preregistered harmful-overrepair counts and paired aggregation using these artifacts and the analysis plan.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation. Within this preregistered controlled-challenge, exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to the repair model produced a substantial increase in verifier+simulator-validated outcomes (approx. +20.51 percentage points; p = 0.02148). The shared controlled-fault pairing (identical initial candidate per pair) isolates the effect of exposing diagnostics under the adapter's shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics: both arms received the same initial candidate and identical repair budgets, so observed differences arise from diagnostic exposure and repair behavior under the adapter contract.

Mechanism and diagnostics. Archived per-episode validator traces (execution/scoring/*.json) show that guarded repairs commonly used specific violation codes to target edits (examples: removing unintended edits to protected interfaces or restoring required command sequences). These traces support a plausible causal pathway from diagnostic exposure to improved verifier outcomes without requiring additional independent first-pass generations.

Safety boundary and preregistered gap. The preregistered harmful-overrepair confirmatory aggregation was not produced by the archived executor and therefore remains unresolved for confirmatory inference. We provide the precise artifact locations and the exact operational mapping used by the scoring pipeline so auditors can reproduce that preregistered safety statistic deterministically from the archive. Until such recomputation is executed and recorded in the archive, we treat harmful-overrepair as an unresolved preregistered safety question.

Operational implications and verifier tax. The experiment is instrumented: hosted-model_call_event_count = 118 and stage_counts are recorded (valid_source_generation = 40; blind_controlled_fault_repair = 39; validator_guided_controlled_fault_repair = 39). These counts enable exploratory computation of model-call cost per avoided failure, but large-scale cost/latency feasibility for deployment remains an open operational question requiring larger-scale study.

Threats to validity. Internal: model sampling nondeterminism (temperature = null in execution/model_configuration.json) and exactly-one initial sampled generation per pair limit claims about generation determinism; pairing semantics are per the registered adapter contract. Construct: primary success depends on verifier+simulator agreement; verifier coverage and simulator fidelity constrain the operational meaning of "valid." External: single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and a synthetic template-based controlled-fault bank limit generality to diverse vendors, models, and live workloads. Conclusion: complete_pairs = 39 yields reasonable precision for the observed primary effect but is underpowered for fine-grained per-fault-class claims; subgroup analyses should be treated as exploratory.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered controlled-fault paired experiment using hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 and shared controlled-fault candidates, exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow increased verifier+simulator-validated configuration success by ~20.51 percentage points (p = 0.021484375; 95% CI [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359]). This effect is bounded by the synthetic task bank, the declared model gpt-5-mini, and the archived deterministic verifier and simulator. A preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair statistic was not produced by the archived confirmatory executor and therefore remains unresolved; the archived per-episode traces and transformation manifest provide the exact inputs for independent recomputation. We release the evidence bundle to enable reproducible reaggregation and recommend multi-model, multi-verifier replications and larger-scale cost/latency studies to evaluate operational feasibility and safety at NetOps scale.

Adapter: hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2. Declared model used for confirmatory execution: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json). Exact initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: f781dd7978328198146d586cf33e0f4b783c8db126bd0f16fcd13699455ebb10) and cited here by immutable archive reference. Human role: a Research Director selected the topic family and pre-lock constraints; after the autonomy lock the autonomous system performed preregistration, experiment execution, analysis, and manuscript generation; no manual human editing of technical manuscript content occurred after the lock. Execution semantics and sampling records: execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null (unset); null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Per-call runtime sampling parameters and provider traces are archived at execution/execution_log.jsonl and execution/provider_calls/*.json. Pairing semantics: exactly one sampled initial generation per task pair was performed and reused by both arms under shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics; baseline denotes blind repair and guarded denotes repair with deterministic validator diagnostics exposed. Harmful-change mapping: the preregistered harmful-change transformation is archived at execution/transformation_manifest.json and per-episode validator traces are archived at execution/scoring/*.json and execution/raw_results.jsonl. The archived artifacts and analysis outputs required to reproduce the preregistered confirmatory and secondary aggregations are provided in the evidence bundle.
limitations: Synthetic controlled-fault task bank: deterministic injected faults do not represent a broad naturalistic distribution of production NetOps incidents; external validity to live operator workloads is limited.
Single-model and single-adapter evaluation: confirmatory execution used only declared_model_version = gpt-5-mini and one adapter family; results do not establish multi-model generality.
Simulator-backed primary success predicate: primary success required agreement of deterministic verifier and simulator; simulator fidelity and verifier coverage constrain construct validity.

Sample size and power: complete_pairs = 39 offers detectability for the observed primary effect but limits precision for subgroup and per-fault-class inference; exploratory subgroup analyses are not confirmatory.
Operational cost/latency unresolved for deployment: the run was instrumented (hosted-model calls recorded) but large-scale operational feasibility (verifier tax tradeoffs) requires larger studies.

Verifier-exploitation and long-horizon agentic pathologies remain possible: the controlled short-horizon repair budget reduces but does not eliminate these risks; broader agentic workflows need additional defenses.

Preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair test not present in archived confirmatory summary: the archived confirmatory analysis executor did not compute the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation; the per-episode traces and transformation manifest required to compute it are archived and available for independent reaggregation, but the preregistered confirmatory safety verdict is therefore unresolved in this paper.
